findings.title: Missing and tampered Live auth tests pass when the socket is accepted

They do not protect this Live provider access/auth boundary. The current production guard is present; this finding concerns missing regression protection, not a demonstrated production bypass.
findings.recommendation: Assert the concrete Quart WebsocketDisconnectError/close code 4003 for both cases, and assert Live session/client creation was not called. Keep unexpected exceptions visible. Add explicit unauthorized-user/expired initData cases at the relevant shared socket boundary.

findings.title: 10 ms deadline can expire before the mocked SDK coroutine starts
findings.evidence: Isolated Windows run `python -m pytest tests/test_memory_query_expansion_timeout.py --override-ini=addopts= --timeout=30 -q` fails at line 32: cancelled Event is unset. app/repos/memory.py starts one deadline before rendering the prompt and awaits run_gemini_override/policy resolution and quota reservation before generate_content. The test patches only client/quota and assumes the SDK has begun within 0.01 seconds; the valid original-query fallback can occur earlier. Parent separately reproduced the same isolated failure on pushed checkout 425563b4 with the updated lock (1 failed in 1.74s); artifacts .codex/test-audit/memory-timeout-isolated.xml and .log. Parent's warm full run passed, so this is an isolated cold-path test synchronization finding, not an inferred runtime defect.
findings.impact: A correct timeout fallback fails depending on cold imports, scheduler granularity and runtime snapshot/cache state; when it passes it does not isolate provider-cancellation from policy-resolution timing.
findings.recommendation: Mock override/policy resolution explicitly, add a started Event for SDK entry, and control time/deadline or use a generous timeout with deterministic synchronization. Test pre-SDK timeout separately from in-flight provider cancellation.
findings.verification: isolated pytest failure; parent independently reproduced on updated lock

findings.title: Voice privacy test passes without invoking its lease or ASR boundary

findings.evidence: The first key fails after 0.03s, first-text budget is 0.05s, and collection is bounded only at 0.2s. findings.evidence: test_parallel_execution_of_multiple_tools supplies immediately completed AsyncMock search/read operations and checks final answer plus each called once. findings.title: Shared media deadline assertions also accept a fresh timeout for the reserve model
findings.evidence: The first model sleeps 0.01s and returns None; the second hangs; the 0.03s configured deadline is guarded only by a 0.3s outer wait. findings.recommendation: Use a controlled clock/record remaining deadline, or release a reserve result after the shared deadline but before a restarted deadline and assert it is rejected. Exercise a first attempt completing within the budget before the reserve for Crocodile; require cleanup in finally.

findings.title: Audio input forwarding test only observes an independent scripted output
findings.evidence: test_audio_forwarding creates send_realtime_input=AsyncMock, sends activity/audio/end frames, but asserts only the connected and audio output frames; it never asserts an SDK call or decoded input payload. findings.title: Database fixtures alter schema and hide setup/cleanup failures
findings.evidence: Both DB fixtures connect, register codec and start transaction before try/finally. Codec/start failure can bypass connection close. They add compatibility columns inside the test transaction, masking missing migrated schema for those fields. Cleanup uses conn.reset for an ordinary active transaction and broadly ignores cleanup exceptions; asyncpg emits reset-with-active-transaction noise. CI migration/schema checks provide separate protection.
findings.impact: Failure diagnosis is noisy; fixture setup can leak a connection and schema tests can silently repair the schema they should inspect.
findings.recommendation: Own connection cleanup immediately after acquisition, roll back a healthy owned transaction explicitly, bound broken-connection cleanup and retain diagnostics. Use the migrated schema without compatibility DDL, or test legacy compatibility explicitly.

findings.title: Sequential-message test wraps a lock locally rather than invoking message processing
findings.evidence: mock_handler_task implements async with state.get_user_lock itself and calls local fake functions. It never invokes the real message handler. findings.title: Optional DB container harness is neither selected by integration CI nor safely scoped
findings.evidence: testcontainers is absent from the locked dev graph, so two horoscope subscription tests skip locally. Those tests have no integration marker and are excluded by -m integration. The session fixture writes DATABASE_URL and app.config settings without restoring them, initializes a singleton async pool via asyncio.run and yields after that loop closes. It uses pg16 whereas CI uses pg17. The activated container path was not executed in this audit.

findings.title: Restoring sys.modules does not undo module reloads performed under mocks
findings.evidence: setUp installs MagicMocks for app.utils and app.utils.metrics_middleware and reloads the existing app.metrics module in place (lines 23–37); tearDown only stops patch.dict (46–48). A narrow offline pytest plugin captured the real pre-test references and found time_utils and MetricsMiddleware still MagicMocks after this passing test, and metrics_collector replaced. Production app/metrics.py imports time_utils at 15 and middleware at 631 and recreates metrics_collector at 627. tests/test_auth_headers.py:62, test_web_security.py:75 and test_menus.py:141/208 also reload existing modules while mocks are installed; their registry teardown cannot undo those objects. test_security_headers.py:59 instead discards an existing app.web without saving it, while its cleanup excludes pre-existing app module keys.
findings.impact: Subsequent tests may exercise fake utilities, new application objects or stale imports. xdist_group co-locates a group and does not provide process exclusivity; serial offline passing results do not prove isolation. The root conftest only repairs settings attributes, so these bindings remain altered.
findings.recommendation: Import application modules with real dependencies, then monkeypatch the specific attributes used by a test in fixture scope. Run genuinely import-time/startup tests in a subprocess or preserve and restore every mutated module object/parent binding and singleton. Add a post-teardown identity check for representative production aliases.
findings.verification: platform-reload-probe.json: test_exitstatus=0, time_utils_is_magicmock=true, MetricsMiddleware_is_magicmock=true, metrics_collector_is_original=false.

findings.title: Reload and singleton resets leave production aliases pointing to different instances
findings.evidence: test_database_module_loads_cleanly reloads app.database solely to check db_query exists. app/database.py:414 constructs a new DatabaseManager after the class is redefined, but app/repos/keys.py:20 imports db_manager by value. tests/test_group_chat.py:11 and :18 reset GroupChatManager._instance without restoring the prior instance; app/group_chat.py exports an already-created group_chat_manager. A safe three-case offline probe passed all cases while keys.db_manager differed from database.db_manager and GroupChatManager._instance differed from group_chat_manager after teardown.
findings.impact: Later repository tests can patch or inspect one manager while module-level wrappers use another; group cache tests can consult a manager different from the one later constructors return. These mismatches undermine fixture isolation and can mask behavior through old aliases.
findings.recommendation: Use a subprocess for clean-import smoke checks instead of reloading a live singleton module. Scope singleton resets with monkeypatch or yield/finally restoration so the original class instance and exported manager remain consistent after every test.

findings.evidence: test_returns_string_with_user_id calls get_waiting_message(user_id=12345) without stubbing personalization or DB access. app/utils/waiting_facts.py:134 uses random.random()<0.3 before get_personalized_stat; its first action at :59 is db.db_query. app/database.py:_execute_with_retry reconnects when the pool is missing. findings.evidence: The test seeds self.cache.qna_cache then patches app.cache.redis_client=None, calls module clear_cache and performs no assertion (73–83). app/cache.py:249–252 returns immediately when Redis is absent; it never receives or accesses that self.cache instance. findings.title: The executor test passes when image processing fails and returns None
findings.evidence: The test patches _image_process_pool with an unconfigured MagicMock, sends invalid image bytes, ignores _result and only asserts the imported _image_worker is not None (77–82). app/utils/image_utils.py:196–205 awaits run_in_executor and catches executor/worker errors by returning None. findings.evidence: All snake-case parameters set should_not_have_italic=True, but the conditional only validates balanced HTML (220–224) and never forbids . _validate_balanced_html ignores every non-Telegram tag (31–32); the special-character case then removes every <...> sequence with a regex before checking angle brackets (264–266). Other exact escaping tests exist in test_text_format.py; this finding concerns the misleading E2E assertions, not a proven current formatter defect.

Reject unsupported tags in the oracle and assert the expected escaped script/bracket text in returned output. Preserve known supported tags without first erasing arbitrary markup from the evidence.

findings.title: The Local Bot API ordering test can pass after the actual release call is removed

findings.title: Redis fencing tests reimplement Lua instead of exercising the scripts used in production
findings.evidence: QueueRedis.eval dispatches by comparison with queue_module's current script constants and executes independent Python ownership/recovery logic (74–108). Changing queue_module._FINISH_TASK to the Lua text 'return 1' still invokes the correct Python owner guard; the double returned 0 for a wrong owner while that Lua would return 1. Production app/queue.py:66–108 contains the actual scripts. Whole-test-corpus rg found no actual eval/evalsha use against a Redis service; the only real Redis.from_url at test_dependency_boundaries.py:254 only reads connection kwargs and closes the client. Daily preparation also uses a Python eval double.
findings.impact: Queue orchestration/interleaving coverage is useful, but syntax, KEYS/ARGV positions, TTL semantics and fencing regressions inside production Lua can pass all these tests. This is a coverage gap, not evidence that the current Lua is broken.
findings.recommendation: Retain deterministic unit doubles for Python control flow and add isolated Redis integration tests executing the exact production constants. Exercise active/expired owner, wrong token, retry/recovery, lease TTL and duplicate disposition using a unique namespace and safe cleanup.
findings.verification: platform-probes.json: redis_double_returns_guarded_zero_for_lua_return_one=true; full corpus searched for Redis.from_url, redis.Redis, redis.asyncio, TEST_REDIS, eval and evalsha.

findings.title: Mocking create_task leaves unscheduled coroutines and fake tasks in the reminder registry
findings.evidence: The two AI dispatch tests patch asyncio.create_task with a plain MagicMock (301 and 330), inspect call count and never await/close the supplied coroutine. Production check_and_deliver_reminders creates _execute_ai_reminder and inserts the returned object into _background_ai_tasks with an add_done_callback (app/handlers/cmd_reminders.py:591–602). A source-extracted execution under these exact conditions retained a coroutine still in its created state and one fake task in the global registry; the done callback never runs.
findings.impact: Tests leave coroutine/task state behind while claiming to verify dispatch. Unawaited coroutine warnings may be suppressed by shared warning policy, and repeated runs accumulate fake task entries.
findings.recommendation: Use a create_task side effect that schedules the supplied coroutine on the real test loop and await/cancel the resulting task under scoped worker mocks. For a scheduling-only contract, capture and close every coroutine in finally and restore the background task registry; also assert the worker arguments/mode rather than only one scheduling call.
findings.verification: platform-probes.json: reminder_create_task_mock_retains_unscheduled_coroutine=true, reminder_mock_task_leaks_in_background_registry=1. The probe closed its captured coroutines after recording facts.

findings.title: Cancellation and limit-one tests can pass without successful acquisition or mutual exclusion
findings.evidence: The cancellation test sleeps 10ms before cancelling, swallows both CancelledError and every ordinary Exception, and only checks the final permit value (70–79). A source-extracted run passed with a semaphore whose __aenter__ raises ValueError before acquiring anything. The limit-one test only asserts sorted entry IDs and final permit count (153–154); the unchanged test passed against a no-limit async context manager with peak concurrency 3.
findings.impact: A broken acquisition path or missing limit-one exclusion can satisfy these named invariant tests. The separate configured-limit-two case measures peak concurrency properly, but it does not make these weaker cases verify their own contracts.
findings.recommendation: Signal an Event immediately after successful acquisition and wait for it before cancelling; require CancelledError with pytest.raises and assert cleanup/permit reuse. For limit one, count active work and assert peak==1 while tasks overlap at a deterministic barrier; do not infer exclusion from the list of tasks that eventually ran.

findings.title: The cached-limit fixture admits a dict in an integer-returning contract
findings.evidence: test_returns_cached_limit seeds _model_config_cache with {'daily_limit':200} and accepts either 200 or that dict (55–58). app/repos/keys.py:239 annotates int|None; its cache hit at :247–248 returns the cached object, and its DB miss path stores the scalar limit at :255–261. Downstream key availability uses the value as a numeric limit. The exact source-extracted cached branch returned the dict and satisfied this permissive assertion.
findings.impact: The test blesses an impossible normal cache shape and a return type that callers cannot use for limit arithmetic; it fails to protect the actual cached-scalar behavior or integer type.
findings.recommendation: Seed the cache with 200 and require result==200 plus no DB query. Add a DB-to-cache second-call roundtrip so the fixture shape comes from the actual writer, and cover None/config override behavior with exact expectations.

findings.title: The invalid-header rejection test never sends the invalid header
findings.evidence: test_invalid_header_token_redirects constructs an invalid X-Auth-Token header but calls client.get(/) at line 161 without a headers argument. It only proves the already-covered unauthenticated request redirects. The adjacent correct-header test passes headers explicitly.
findings.impact: Accepting an arbitrary nonempty X-Auth-Token would not be detected by this named rejection case; it never reaches the invalid-header branch.
findings.recommendation: Pass headers=headers to the request and assert the expected rejection/redirect. For protected API routes also require 401 with an incorrect token, and ensure no protected handler/DB work is invoked.

findings.title: WebSocket rejection tests can pass on wrong route, success, or arbitrary server error
findings.evidence: test_missing_init_data uses /webapp/ws although app/web_miniapp.py:2513 registers /game/ws under /webapp. Lines 43–47 and 54–58 swallow every Exception and have no rejection assertion. A successfully received message also exits without failure.
findings.impact: Auth and missing-game regressions are invisible; the missing-initData case currently exercises a nonexistent route rather than the game handler.
findings.recommendation: Use /webapp/game/ws and require the concrete Quart WebsocketDisconnectError/response for the current close contract. Assert close/status code and ensure unexpected exceptions or an accepted frame fail.

findings.title: Restart test replaces both persistence functions with its own serializer
findings.evidence: test_topic_scoped_generated_words_survive_restart_and_ignore_other_topic defines _persist_generated_words_for_test and _load_generated_words_from_disk_for_test at 277–284 and monkeypatches the real functions at 286–289. Production app/games/judgement_cache.py:430–456 handles UTF-8 files, atomic replace and load capacity; none executes.
findings.impact: A no-op or broken production load/write path still passes the test advertised as restart persistence. Other test_games.py generated-word cases patch persistence to no-ops too.
findings.recommendation: Point _DATA_DIR/_GEN_WORDS_CACHE_PATH at tmp_path, keep the real persist/load functions, clear only the process store, and assert the loaded words/topic isolation and on-disk payload.

findings.title: Image enhancement test patches nonexistent symbols and explicitly passes when generator never runs
findings.evidence: Test uses create=True for app.games.crocodile_daily.get_pollinations_provider and app.games.crocodile_daily_telegram._upload_image_to_telegram; current implementation imports get_pollinations_provider locally from app.providers.pollinations at app/games/crocodile_daily.py:376 and uploads with bot.send_photo at 528. It passes string puzzle_date='2024-01-01' at test line 73, swallows AttributeError at 75–76, and executes assert True when its mock was never called at 78–84. _daily_image_seed requires date.strftime at source 295.
findings.impact: The test is green without reaching the provider, so enhance/negative-prompt regressions are untested. Wrong-target create=True masks refactoring and date-type errors.
findings.recommendation: Patch app.providers.pollinations.get_pollinations_provider, pass date(...), use a result object with success/images/warning/model_used and a Telegram bot boundary fake; require assert_awaited_once and inspect actual kwargs unconditionally.

findings.title: Rejected-model tests assert against obsolete settings writer
findings.evidence: Negative settings tests at 830–881 patch app.repos.settings_repo.set_global_setting and require assert_not_awaited, but llm_model persistence now calls app.runtime_settings.processes.save_primary_model at app/web.py:1757. The old writer at web.py:1765 is only for delivery_enabled. Successful tests correctly patch save_primary_model at 810/764. Same stale negative writer assertion occurs tests/test_daily_croc_models.py:123–130; model persistence calls save_croc_model at web.py:1218. These writers persist through runtime_settings.store (processes.py:32; legacy_models.py:37-41), not set_global_setting.
findings.impact: These tests do check error status, but their claimed no-save guarantee does not observe the actual write boundary. A premature save followed by an error return can pass the negative assertion.
findings.recommendation: Patch the actual model writer for rejection cases and assert_not_awaited (save_primary_model/save_croc_model), keeping independent delivery setting checks where relevant.

findings.title: Database subscription tests are unmarked integration tests behind an optional container dependency
findings.evidence: Tests at 61 and 92 execute INSERT and repository DB operations via postgres_container, but have only asyncio marks, no integration mark. Parent confirmed uv.lock/dev does not include optional testcontainers. The unit CI excludes tests/integration but includes these; integration CI selects -m integration and never selects them.
findings.impact: Real subscription UPSERT/timezone behavior can remain skipped in both regular jobs even while reported unit/integration suites are green.
findings.recommendation: Mark/move these as integration tests and bind them to the repository's explicit isolated TEST_DATABASE_URL fixture/job, or provision/test the declared optional container dependency in a dedicated job. Missing services should be reported as skipped coverage.

findings.title: Oversized-publication guard can pass after attempted forbidden Telegraph publication
findings.evidence: test_create_natal_report_skips_oversized_telegraph_mirror replaces create_telegraph_page_from_markdown with a function raising AssertionError at 150–153, then only checks telegraph_url None and saved report count. Production _try_publish_telegraph wraps the publish call in except Exception (app/natal/service.py:127–139), which also catches this AssertionError and returns None.
findings.impact: Removing the oversized Markdown guard would still make this test pass; the no-publication contract is not established by an exception that production suppresses.
findings.recommendation: Use AsyncMock and assert_not_awaited after create_natal_report, or record calls independently and assert no call. Keep result/storage assertions as separate recovery guarantees.

findings.title: Two LLM repair tests accept fallback output after swallowed test assertions
findings.evidence: test_generate_interpretation_repairs_abstract_language_without_technical_note increments router.calls before asserting the repair prompt in FakeRouter at lines 770-775, then checks only calls == 2 and absence of two abstract phrases at 784-787. test_generate_interpretation_repairs_incomplete_practical_structure similarly asserts the repair prompt inside FakeRouter at 848 and only checks calls, section IDs and absence of the original response at 857-862. app/natal/llm.py:232-234 catches Exception, including AssertionError, and returns _fallback_sections; fallback has these section IDs and lacks both abstract/original phrases. Thus a wrong repair prompt can fail its assertion internally yet leave both tests green. The adjacent repairs_technical_and_overly_abstract_language test requires its distinctive provider phrase at line 716 and does not share that weakness.
findings.impact: Regressions in repair-prompt instructions or failures processing the repaired response can appear as successful LLM repairs even though the service delivered its basic fallback.
findings.recommendation: Capture both request kwargs and assert the repair prompt after generate_interpretation returns. Require a distinctive phrase or exact relevant section from the second provider response and explicitly exclude the fallback marker.

findings.title: The friendly decryption-message test mocks the entire behavior it claims to check
findings.evidence: The test replaces ProviderRouter.get_response with the expected safe message literal and asserts substrings/privacy of that same literal. app/agent_use_cases.py:424–432 simply delegates to router.get_response; no DecryptionError or decryption_failed resolution is induced. The real message is selected by app/providers/router.py:352–357, which the test bypasses. Other tests in this file do verify real key-resolution failure behavior.
findings.impact: A regression in the actual router decryption branch or its user-facing message leaves this case green; as written it only exercises tuple forwarding through the compatibility wrapper.
findings.recommendation: Either rename this as a delegation test and assert router call arguments, or use the real router with key resolution returning decryption_failed and assert the actual error tag/message, token None and absence of sensitive internals. Do not hardcode the answer at the boundary being verified.

findings.title: Short wall-clock limits make functional concurrency regressions depend on host scheduling
findings.evidence: The callback scenario gives user A a 300ms sleep, delays 20ms to assume lock acquisition and requires B to complete within 150ms (69–83). The circuit-breaker concurrency test requires five 100ms sleeps to finish below 300ms (test_circuit_breaker_concurrency.py:37–46), although it already has a stronger max_in_flight==5 assertion at :49. No source/probe claim establishes current flakiness; the review identifies scheduling-sensitive functional oracles.
findings.impact: A busy CI worker, debugger or slow process can fail otherwise correct functional behavior, while the initial sleep does not prove A acquired the lock. This adds noisy failures to concurrency contracts.
findings.recommendation: Use acquired/release Events to prove B completes while A still holds its user lock, with a generous outer timeout only to detect hangs. Keep measured peak concurrency for the breaker and own its monitor cleanup; isolate true performance benchmarks from these functional cases.

findings.title: Some resource-owning tests do not dispose resources on their failure paths
findings.evidence: test_taskmanager_bounded_and_drain only clears tm._tasks in finally; if an assertion before release_event.set fails, the live tasks lose ownership without cancellation/awaiting. test_circuit_breaker_concurrency constructs a breaker in an active loop, whose constructor starts _monitor_task (app/circuit_breaker.py:69–75), and never calls shutdown. The PDF/Word path tests in test_io_handlers.py:15/:46 create OS temporary files with mkstemp and never unlink them; app/document_processor.py:53–111 treats the path as caller-owned and does not delete it.
findings.impact: When a regression occurs, these tests can add pending-task/resource warnings or orphan temporary files and obscure the original failure. Successful normal paths do not validate fixture cleanup reliability.
findings.recommendation: Keep ownership until every task is cancelled and awaited in finally, always release test barriers, and call breaker.shutdown in finally or a yield fixture. Use tmp_path or explicit finally unlink for caller-owned PDF/Word inputs. The cancellation-resistant drain test later in test_taskmanager_bounded.py already demonstrates proper Event release and awaited cleanup.

findings.title: Debounce coalescing test relies on a 200 ms wall-time margin and lacks unconditional cleanup
findings.evidence: test_result_refresh_coalesces_multiple_queue_calls waits asyncio.sleep(2.2) then asserts calls==1. Production debounce is 2.0 at app/games/crocodile_daily_telegram.py:17/484; queued task may start late under loaded xdist. reset_daily_telegram_state_for_tests at 504 runs only after assertion success; root conftest resets ordinary Crocodile Telegram state, not this daily state.
findings.impact: A correct implementation can fail when its debounce task starts >200 ms late, and failure can leave pending work/state for the next test. The suite also spends a real 2.2 seconds here unnecessarily.
findings.recommendation: Use an Event in fake_get_messages to observe actual completion with a generous safety timeout; control _REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_S or an explicit clock/gate and drain/cancel queued tasks in finally/fixture teardown.
